findings.statement: CA9 is tumor-cell intrinsic: RCC cells hold 0.976 of tissue transcripts (54.7% of RCC cells express it; cpm_share 0.958), and tumor cells vs proximal tubule give log2FC 7.739 (padj 0.0189, 6 donors). Bulk signal survives extrapolation to purity 1 (rna_lfc_at_purity1 7.787).

In Visium, high-CA9 spots are enriched for RCC neighbours (log2 enrichment 0.381, padj 0.0017; observed 0.4757 vs expected 0.3654) and weakly for macrophages (log2 0.099, padj 0.0017). The composition-corrected in situ share of CA9 transcripts is 0.999 RCC.

CA9 best glue-site score is only 0.546 (cavity volume 126.8 A3, pocket pLDDT 90.3, 1 accessible lysine); ligand-site recall is 0.5 with recall_in_top_pockets 0.221, and mean model pLDDT is 76.56. This is a modest site, not evidence that a glue exists. CA9 is already addressed by antibody approaches (girentuximab, Phase 3).

CD70 is up in ccRCC bulk (TCGA log2FC 7.09) and stays high at purity 1 (rna_lfc_at_purity1 4.278), supporting tumor-intrinsic expression. Single-cell shows RCC cells as the strongest per-cell expressers, but CD8 T cells hold a larger transcript share because of cell number, so some CD70 signal is lymphocyte-derived. Clinical agents include vorsetuzumab and cusatuzumab (Phase 1 to 2).
KDR is an endothelial gene, not a tumor-cell target: endothelium holds 0.951 of tumor transcripts (40.5% of endothelial cells express it; cpm_share 0.979).

KDR has the second-highest MGD site score in the ranking (0.841): pocket volume 361.1 A3, pocket pLDDT 83.1, 7 accessible lysines. Caveats: ligand-site recall is 0.4 (recall_in_top_pockets 0.2) and mean model pLDDT is 71.12. The cell target would be endothelium.

CD74 is an antigen-presenting immune gene, not a tumor-cell target: cDC are 100% positive and macrophages 99.5%, and macrophages carry 0.436 of tissue transcripts. CD8 T cells also hold 0.345 of transcripts (95.5% positive) because of their numbers.
CXCR4 is lymphocyte-borne: CD8 T cells hold 0.563 of transcripts (72.9% express) and CD4 T cells 87.8% express it (transcript share 0.176). It is not tumor-cell intrinsic.
MET transcripts are mainly in tumor cells: RCC holds 0.935 of tissue transcripts (35.2% of cells express it; cpm_share 0.682), with a minor endothelial contribution (12% of cells, cpm_share 0.283).

EPAS1 transcripts in this scRNA-seq are mostly stromal: endothelium holds 0.365 of transcripts (81.3% express; cpm_share 0.626) and fibroblasts 70.3% express it, while RCC cells show 4.9% expressing and 0.051 transcript share. A bulk EPAS1 signal therefore cannot be read as tumor-intrinsic from these data.
EGFR transcripts sit in tumor cells: RCC holds 0.948 of tissue transcripts (29.7% of cells express it; cpm_share 0.542), with a minor fibroblast and endothelial contribution.

SCARB1 is up in bulk (TCGA log2FC 3.989; rna_lfc_at_purity1 3.762), but single-cell is mixed: macrophages hold 0.384 of transcripts, RCC 0.336 and endothelium 0.116, with endothelium the highest per cell (cpm_share 0.406). Treat as a shared tumor, myeloid and endothelial signal, with no clinical drug listed.
NNMT ranks 7th in convergence: up in TCGA (log2FC 4.685), robust at purity 1 (rna_lfc_at_purity1 5.256), with adverse prognosis (cox log HR 0.301, padj 0.00479). No clinical drug is listed.

ALDOB is a loss-of-expression biomarker: down in TCGA (log2FC -4.741) and at purity 1 (rna_lfc_at_purity1 -6.302); lower expression goes with worse survival (cox log HR -0.358). Because it is down, it is not a tumor-cell target.

COL23A1 is the top tumor-track first-in-class candidate (novelty 0.767): RCC cells hold 0.881 of tumor transcripts, 7 ccRCC papers, no clinical drug, antibody/PROTAC-tractable, surface or secreted, max vital-organ nTPM 3 (heart muscle). Replicated in TCGA (log2FC 5.829) and purity-robust (rna_lfc_at_purity1 4.88). Its AlphaFold model is low confidence (mean pLDDT 58.91) and the best glue site scores only 0.2342 (volume 8.0 A3). Hypothesis only: no dependency evidence (DepMap mean effect 0.167, not selective) and literature is counted by gene symbol.

RAB42 is the second tumor-track candidate (novelty 0.705): RCC holds 0.627 of tumor transcripts, only 2 ccRCC papers, no clinical drug, max vital-organ nTPM 2.6 (lung). TCGA log2FC 4.371 and rna_lfc_at_purity1 3.189 support tumor-intrinsic expression. Its best glue site is small (score 0.5348, volume 37.4 A3), so it is weak. Hypothesis only: no selective dependency (DepMap mean effect -0.075).

OLFML2A is a stromal (fibroblast) discovery candidate, a microenvironment target and not a tumor-cell target: fibroblasts hold 0.647 of tumor transcripts, 2 ccRCC papers, no clinical drug, antibody-tractable. TCGA log2FC 2.372 and rna_lfc_at_purity1 1.527. Caveat: colon expression is nTPM 27.9 (vital-organ risk) and there is no functional or dependency evidence.

GAL3ST4 is the top immune-track candidate (novelty 0.64): macrophages hold 0.972 of tumor transcripts, 1 ccRCC paper, no clinical drug. It is up in TCGA (log2FC 2.993) with purity-1 log2FC 0.401 and adverse prognosis (cox log HR 0.177). Its best glue site scores 0.7874 (volume 819.7 A3, 5 accessible lysines, pocket pLDDT 92.8, model pLDDT 79.31) but no ligand-site validation is available. A macrophage target, not a tumor-cell one; hypothesis only.

LILRB4 is a macrophage-held immune candidate (0.933 of tumor transcripts, 7 ccRCC papers, no clinical drug) but flagged infiltration-driven: TCGA log2FC 3.7 shrinks to 0.508 at purity 1 and it is not purity-robust. Its bulk signal reflects immune infiltration, not tumor-cell expression.

caveats: Discovery candidates are data-ranked hypotheses: none has dependency or functional evidence, and literature counts are by gene symbol.
MGD scores rank sites only; they do not show that a glue exists or would work. Ligand-site recall is modest (0.4 to 0.5) where it could be checked and is unavailable for the discovery genes.
scRNA-seq cell counts differ widely by cell type (e.g. many CD8 T cells, few endothelial cells), so transcript share is read together with cpm_share.
CD70 and NNMT single-cell records carried no evidence ids, so their cell-level numbers are not quoted; CD70 is not covered by the Visium sections.
Endothelium and PT cell counts are small (39 PT cells from 1 donor), limiting tumor-vs-PT comparisons.
